precepts.text: Of the children of Issachar, which were men that had understanding of the times, to know what Israel ought to do. They were able to read the stars and lead the ships; they knew how to navigate the waters.
precepts.point: Semitic primarily refers to a major language family of the Middle East and the Horn of Africa which includes Hebrew, Arabic, and Aramaic: the people of Shem. But when it comes to the Israelites, the Most High is only dealing with the twelve tribes.

note.label: 250 Years of Celebration 400 Years of Sweat Equity (Pt 2)

precepts.why:
“For the most High then shewed signs for them, and held still the flood, till they were passed over.” The tribes that left the heathen went into the Euphrates “by the narrow places of the river” and down into the ocean, and the Most High was with them. He showed them signs, and there were men among them able to read those signs.

“And of the children of Issachar, which were men that had understanding of the times, to know what Israel ought to do; the heads of them were two hundred; and all their brethren were at their commandment.” Issachar could read the stars. That is how they were the navigators: they had understanding of the times, they knew what Israel ought to do, and so they were able to lead the ships as the tribes came over. They knew how to navigate the waters.

They understood the winds and the currents, the Atlantic drift routes from Africa to America. Solomon understood all of this too, with the navy he had going out; the same ports Solomon’s navy knew were the stops along the route, because “through that country there was a great way to go, namely, of a year and a half”. African boatmen from Lake Chad later built a papyrus boat on the pattern of the ancient Egyptians and sailed it from North Africa as far as Barbados, proving such a drift journey on the Africa-to-America currents could be done, because the currents were understood.

So the ten tribes did not wander blindly into “a further country, where never mankind dwelt”. The Most High showed signs, Issachar read them, and the ships came across into the region called Arsareth, the land Columbus identified with America. “Then dwelt they there until the latter time”, and that is why we are here in the latter times.

precepts.text: Benjamin stood with its own against all Israel, showing the tribal loyalty David feared.
precepts.point: The spirit came upon Amasai, chief of the captains, who said, "Thine are we, David, and on thy side, thou son of Jesse: peace be unto thee, for thy God helpeth thee." David received them and made them captains.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 12: The Tribes Gather to David

precepts.why:
The tribes of Israel sent through all Benjamin asking, “What wickedness is this that is done among you?” and told them to deliver up “the men, the children of Belial, which are in Gibeah, that we may put them to death, and put away evil from Israel.” “But the children of Benjamin would not hearken to the voice of their brethren the children of Israel”. Instead they “gathered themselves together out of the cities unto Gibeah, to go out to battle against the children of Israel.”

Benjamin stood with its own against all Israel. Benjamin tended to stick with Benjamin, and that is the tribal loyalty David feared. So when “there came of the children of Benjamin and Judah to the hold unto David”, he was leery because of the beef between him and Saul. He went out to meet them and said, “If ye be come peaceably unto me to help me, mine heart shall be knit unto you: but if ye be come to betray me to mine enemies, seeing there is no wrong in mine hands, the God of our fathers look thereon, and rebuke it.”

Then the spirit came upon Amasai, chief of the captains: “Thine are we, David, and on thy side, thou son of Jesse”. So “David received them, and made them captains of the band.”

precepts.text: The harvest is plenteous but the labourers few; pray the Lord to send forth labourers, and keep working while He adds to you.
precepts.point: Day by day men came to David until it was a great host like the host of God. When the Most High works with you He sends help, as Christ said to pray for more labourers while continuing the work.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 12: The Tribes Gather to David

precepts.why:
Christ said, “The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few; Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest.” Pray for more labourers, and keep working while He adds to you.

That is what happened to David. Captains of the thousands of Manasseh fell to him at Ziklag and helped him “against the band of the rovers: for they were all mighty men of valour”. “For at that time day by day there came to David to help him, until it was a great host, like the host of God.” When the Most High works with you, He sends help.

precepts.text: The Most High breathed on the slain and they lived and stood upon their feet, an exceeding great army, which is what He has made of Israel.
precepts.point: To keep rank is to stay in proper order and play your role without jockeying for position. They were not double minded but listened to orders and structure. When we battle the wickedness of this world we must keep our rank; it is imperative.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 12: The Tribes Gather to David

precepts.why:
“So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army.” The Most High breathed on the slain and they lived, and that is what He has made of Israel: an exceeding great army.

An army has to keep rank. Of Zebulun there were fifty thousand, “expert in war, with all instruments of war”, “which could keep rank: they were not of double heart.” To keep rank is to stay in proper order and play your role without jockeying for position. They were not double minded; they listened to orders and structure.

When we battle the wickedness of this world, we must keep our rank. It is imperative.

precepts.text: Israel is to be of one accord, perfectly joined together in the same mind and judgment.
precepts.point: They were with David three days eating and drinking, and their brethren brought bread, figs, raisins, wine, oil, and cattle abundantly, for there was joy in Israel. The joy came from being of one mind, which is why the feast days are to be kept with gladness.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 12: The Tribes Gather to David

precepts.why:
“Now I beseech you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that ye all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you; but that ye be perfectly joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment.” Israel is to be of one accord.

That is what the tribes were at Hebron. The men of war “came with a perfect heart to Hebron, to make David king over all Israel: and all the rest also of Israel were of one heart to make David king.” Even the tribes beyond Jordan were of one accord with the rest. That is why we must be of one accord, for Christ is going to sit on the throne of David his father.

They were with David three days, eating and drinking, and their brethren brought bread, figs, raisins, wine, oil and cattle abundantly, “for there was joy in Israel.” The joy came from being of one mind, which is why the feast days are to be kept with gladness.
